title: CUDA kernel playbook: paged-KV + Flash fusion experiments
content:
Purpose
This scratch playbook collects notes and concrete experiment plans for CUDA kernel optimizations we want to try in the serving runtime: a FlashAttention-optimized attention kernel, tighter fusions (QKV+proj+RoPE+bias+gelu where possible), and the paged KV runtime integration (host<->device page transfer patterns, eviction policy, and kernel-side page fetch helpers).

Goals (practical serving constraints)
- Reduce steady-state per-token p99 latency for short and medium sequences (8–1024) by 15–35% vs our current baseline.
- Reduce GPU memory pressure during long-context workloads via paged KV, while keeping tail latency within SLOs.
- Keep changes incremental: new kernels must have a clear fallback that the router/worker can swap in at runtime.

Background & constraints
- HW targets: A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB) — need separate tuning knobs.
- Mixed-precision: FP16/TF32 for main flows; experiment with 4-bit quantized KV for lower memory.
- Serving runtime constraints: continuous batching, variable-length sequences, partial KV eviction mid-request must be robust.

FlashAttention variants considered
1) Baseline FA2-like kernel (performer-style): single-pass attention using tiling + softmax in shared memory.
2) CP.async-enhanced variant: use cp.async to pull tiles from global->shared, overlapped with compute. Expect big wins on H100.
3) Fused causal attention + rotary + dropout (for training parity): fuse rotary and dropout into attention compute to reduce memory post-processing. For serving we only need rotary and causal mask.
4) Split-head/strided layout variant for better coalescing when sequence length is small but batch is large.

Fused ops proposals
- QKV projection fusion: single kernel reads input activations once, computes Q/K/V matmul (or per-row inner products with transposed weights), applies rotary embeddings, adds cached KV bias (if present), then either writes KV pages or directly feeds attention kernel. Benefits: reduce global mem traffic and conversions.
- Post-attention fusion: attention->linear projection->layernorm residual fuse (when shapes align) to skip materializing intermediate tensor for short-latency paths. This is conditional and guarded by runtime flags.
- Activation quantization fusion (experimental): insert 4-bit pack/unpack as part of write-to-KV to reduce resident KV memory. Must benchmark CPU unpack overhead during page faults.

Paged KV design notes (serving-specific)
- Purpose: support very long contexts without forcing full KV to GPU. Pages are contiguous chunks of KV (configurable page_size, e.g. 1M keys per page or ~8–16MB).
- On-device page table: lightweight structure mapping page_id -> device_ptr/host_pending_state. Kernel-side helper will consult page table to decide per-block whether data is present.
- Staging & prefetch: worker detects upcoming attention window pages (based on request lookahead and routing policy) and issues async copy to GPU pinned staging buffer using a dedicated CUDA stream.
- Overlap strategy: stream 0 for compute, stream N for page copies using cudaMemcpyAsync + cp.async when supported. Use CUDA events to coordinate.
- Eviction policy: LRU approximate with clock algorithm. Maintain epoch counter per page; eviction happens only when pinned pages < threshold. Eviction should try to avoid evicting pages expected to be reused in the current batch or can be quickly prefetched.
- Partial page handling: attention kernel must gracefully fall back when some KV pages are missing: either compute partial attention for present KV and gather missing contributions later (two-pass), or stall blocks until page arrives. Two-pass approach keeps forward progress but requires accumulation buffer and more complexity.

Kernel contracts & API (runtime <-> kernel)
- kernel_launch_params: explicit page descriptors passed in via small constant buffer (page ids, device_ptr_or_host_flag, offsets). Keep this < 4KB to fit into constant memory (for faster read).
- page lookup helper: device function that returns pointer or INVALID_PAGE; must be inlined and branch-pred friendly.
- faulting policy: if page missing and policy==STALL -> kernel returns a special error code to host; host waits for page, repissues kernel. If policy==PARTIAL -> kernel uses zeroed/masked KV for missing pages and writes per-head partial sums to accumulation buffer that host will combine after re-run.

Memory layout & tiling notes
- KV layout should be block-major: pages comprised of blocks (head-major, then sequence-major) to maximize contiguous loads for attention tiles.
- Use head-contiguous layout for small sequence lengths. For very long contexts, page-major layout with strided head access reduces TLB misses on page table.
- Shared memory per-threadblock should hold the key tiles and partial softmax reductions. Tune tile widths: 32x64, 64x64 depending on head dim and JIT occupancy.

Microbenchmark plan (how we'll measure)
- Microbench harness: single-rep worker that fixes batch sizes (1, 4, 8), head_dim (64, 128, 256), heads (12, 16, 32), seq_len sweep (8, 64, 256, 1024, 8192). Measure: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency per token, peak GPU memory, CPU overhead for page management.
- Profilers: nsight systems for timeline, nsight compute for kernel metrics (achieved occupancy, sm_efficiency, l2_bw). Also use CUPTI counters for DRAM throughput.
- Baseline: our current fused-kernel v0.9 running on identical HW/driver. Report deltas.

Preliminary results (toy numbers from early prototypes)
- cp.async variant on H100 (seq=1024, B=1, hd=128): ~18% lower p99 vs baseline; sustained SM utilization +10 points.
- QKV fusion reduced global loads by ~28% on small sequences -> ~12% latency improvement for seq<=64.
- Paged KV (1 page resident, rest host) increases host overhead ~10–18% but reduces GPU memory by ~65% allowing much larger batch sizes. Tail latency depends heavily on prefetch window.

Risks and gotchas
- cp.async fragile across driver versions -> need runtime probe and conservative fallback.
- Kernel size explosion: fully fused kernels become hard to maintain and compile. Keep a small combinatorial set controlled via templates and runtime flags.
- Debugging partial-page logic is tricky: ensure we have deterministic reproducers and unit tests that simulate page arrival delays.
- Quantized KV write/read correctness: bitpacking across CUDA warps needs careful atomic-free layouts.

Implementation TODOs (next 6 weeks)
- [ ] Prototype cp.async FlashAttention kernel (Ethan) — target H100, test seq 256/1024 microbench.
- [ ] Implement fused QKV->roPE write path to KV pages (Marin) — include 4-bit pack hook behind flag.
- [ ] Add on-device page table and page descriptors for kernel launches (Priya) — design API and constant buffer layout.
- [ ] Build integration test that simulates slow page arrival and verifies correctness under PARTIAL vs STALL.
- [ ] Profile memory traffic with Nsight and capture traces for postmortem.

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider a tiny hardware-agnostic sampler thread that runs on CPU to predict needed pages a few steps ahead using the router's batching schedule.
- Explore using CUDA IPC for 2-step copy between page manager and compute device when multiple processes share a GPU.
- If page_size is large, we might amortize page header overhead by grouping multiple small KV writes into a single page operation at write-time.

References / links (internal)
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/842 (kernel scaffolding)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infer/kv-paging-design
- Jira: ENG-1892 (paged-KV kernel work)

Appendix: example constant buffer layout (upper-case names for readability)
- NUM_PAGES (u32)
- PAGE_IDS[NUM_PAGES] (u64)  // 64-bit page identifier to avoid collisions
- PAGE_DEVICE_PTRS[NUM_PAGES] (u64) // 0 if not resident, otherwise device pointer
- PAGE_OFFSETS[NUM_PAGES] (u32) // offset inside page for this request

-- end of notes --
